topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
Next steps and exec readout scheduling
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Ivy Morales (Redwood CSM); Aisha Rahman (Northbridge Head of Product), Diego Torres (ML Eng), Emily Zhao (Security), Carlos Mendez (Ops), Samir Patel (Finance)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio good?
[00:05] Aisha Rahman: Yep, good here.
[00:08] Marcus Chen: Great. I can kick off with the bench highlights — I'll keep it short, then we'll go into success criteria alignment.
[00:15] Marcus Chen: Ok slide deck, uh, slide 3 — this was the final tuned run we did last night. Remember baseline was the open model hosted on our cluster with default quant flags. The tuned run used int8 quant, prefix KV caching enabled, and a slightly higher batch target for throughputs. Results were: p50 latency ~140 ms, p95 ~360 ms for the 128 token target, and token throughput roughly 18 tps. We saw cost per 1k tokens drop by about 22% versus baseline.
[00:38] Diego Torres: Sorry quick interrupt — when you say p95 360 ms that's with the larger context window? We usually test with mixed lengths so just want to be sure.
[00:45] Marcus Chen: Good call. This run was weighted to your traffic profile — 60% short messages (<=32 tokens), 30% mid (32-128), 10% long (>128). The p95 includes the tails; for just <=32 tokens p95 was ~240 ms.
[01:05] Aisha Rahman: Mm, ok that's helpful. From a UX standpoint p95 ~240 on short messages is acceptable. For our care agent flow we care more about the short-mid.
[01:12] Lena Park: Also note the dedicated config with reserved capacity would bring p95 for short messages down into the 120-180 ms range but cost will increase — that's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff.
[01:24] Carlos Mendez: Can you quantify "increase"? Samir needs hard numbers for the business case.
[01:29] Samir Patel: Yeah please. We need delta TCO per month, not just percent.
[01:33] Marcus Chen: Absolutely — high level: moving from hosted mixed-tenant to a small dedicated pool for your expected QPS raises infra cost by ~38% but reduces per-token latency by roughly 35% in our model. I'll attach the cost sheet with month-by-month and 12-month NPV rows.
[01:52] Emily Zhao: A few security questions up front — on the private deployment you showed KMS integration. Is customer-managed KMS supported on the on-prem? And do you surface audit logs to our SIEM?
[02:03] Lena Park: Short answer: yes to both. Private/VPC supports bring-your-own KMS (we have HSM integrations for on-prem bundles), and audit logs can be exported to your splunk or whatever SIEM through our logging connector. We will send the security whitepaper with exact endpoints.
[02:22] Emily Zhao: Great. Also need to confirm retention windows and whether logs contain raw prompt text — that's a blocker for us.
[02:29] Marcus Chen: By default hosted redwood masks prompts for analytics; in private you control retention and you can disable storing raw prompts. We'll capture the exact configuration options in the doc.
[02:40] Aisha Rahman: Ok back to success criteria — last time we sketched top-level success as 1) model accuracy parity with baseline (>95% of current acceptance), 2) latency p95 <= 300 ms for short-mid flows, and 3) unit cost under $X per 1k tokens. Can we lock these?
[02:58] Diego Torres: For accuracy, our eval set is small. We want to run 10k samples through tomorrow's run and compare F1 and pass/fail thresholds.
[03:07] Lena Park: Sounds good. Action: Diego to confirm dataset slice. Marcus to run that 10k evaluation and produce the eval report.
[03:14] Diego Torres: Yep I can do that — I'll confirm the slice by EOD Friday.
[03:18] Marcus Chen: I will schedule the runs. Also note we saw a few failure modes with long contexts where KV cache invalidation caused repeated attention recompute — might need a small tweak to the cache TTL.
[03:32] Speaker 1: Mm-hmm.
[03:33] Marcus Chen: Sorry that was me.
[03:35] Aisha Rahman: Can you explain that in plain terms? Diego and I aren't always deep infra.
[03:40] Marcus Chen: Sure — when context windows get long the runtime will evict KV cache entries if the TTL is low; evictions cause more compute on the next request which spikes latency. We increased TTL in the tuned run which smoothed tail latency for long flows, though it slightly increased memory footprint.
[03:57] Carlos Mendez: Memory footprint on dedicated GPUs — is that manageable? What GPUs are we talking about?
[04:03] Marcus Chen: For these runs we used A10G-equivalent in our dedicated pool. Memory rise was about 10% not huge. For on-prem you can pick instance types or scale the pool.
[04:15] Samir Patel: Going back to the business case — what about fallback strategies if peak traffic spikes cause higher latencies? We can't have Service level misses during triage windows.
[04:26] Lena Park: There are three levers: auto-burst capacity you can enable on Dedicated, routing to cheaper hosted model variants for non-critical paths, or graceful degradation (shorter responses / top-k reduction). We can model outage risk into the SLA.
[04:40] Emily Zhao: For regulatory reasons, we need model outputs to be audit-trailed with which model version generated the response. Is that in the logs?
[04:47] Marcus Chen: Yes we add model version id, config flags (quantization, batch size), and request-id. We can correlate that to your transcripts.
[04:55] Aisha Rahman: One concern: latency numbers in the deck were great, but what about cold-starts and scale-up behavior? Our traffic is bursty in the mornings.
[05:05] Marcus Chen: We measured cold-starts — cold VM + warm runtime is around 6-8 seconds for a fresh node; once warmed the steady state is as reported. Autoscaling warm-up can be tuned — we can pre-warm a small buffer for known peaks.
[05:19] Diego Torres: Can you share the exact autoscale policy you used for those runs?
[05:23] Marcus Chen: I'll export the autoscale config as part of the artifacts.
[05:26] Ivy Morales (CSM): Quick check from a process standpoint: are we aligned to do the exec readout as the pilot close? Who needs to attend from Redwood?
[05:35] Lena Park: AE + SE + Product leader ideally. I'll be present. Marcus should present the results. We can bring a solution architect if Emily needs more security detail.
[05:44] Aisha Rahman: Our CTO wants a short business-case deck and risk register. Can Redwood produce a 1-pager cost/benefit with suggested deployment path?
[05:52] Lena Park: Yes. We'll produce a 1-pager and a risk register.
[05:56] Samir Patel: Cost modeling assumptions are important — please include token volumes, QPS, expected growth, reserved capacity amortization, and license fees.
[06:06] Marcus Chen: We'll include a 12-month TCO and a sensitivity table for +/-20% QPS.
[06:12] Emily Zhao: On the compliance checklist — besides SOC2, we need details on data residency and contractual DPA language. Who on Redwood handles legal?
[06:20] Lena Park: I'll loop in our legal and security folks. We'll share standard DPA and regional residency options.
[06:26] Aisha Rahman: Alright let's pivot to the run-by-run notes — Marcus?
[06:30] Marcus Chen: Sure. Run A was baseline, Run B was tuned quant + KV, Run C was dedicated small pool. Observations: Run B lowered cost but had slightly higher p95 on long tails, Run C improved tails significantly. Also saw a small regression in hallucination rate on one prompt family in Run B; that triggered an eval. For the hallucination case we determined it was prompt formatting — Diego is updating the prompt template.
[06:58] Diego Torres: Yes I found a tokenizer mismatch between our preprocessing and the model tokenization, that inflated a prefix and caused stray completions. Fix is rolling out now.
[07:09] Aisha Rahman: Good catch.
[07:12] Marcus Chen: On the model side, we also tried a quantization profile that kept activations in fp16 for the top layers which improved quality at the cost of small memory bump. That might be a middle-ground option.
[07:25] Lena Park: Would you consider that acceptable if it reduces hallucination and keeps cost within your threshold?
[07:31] Samir Patel: If it keeps unit cost under the threshold in the model, yes — we need the numbers.
[07:35] Marcus Chen: We'll include a ternary table: quality / cost / latency for three profiles: baseline, int8 aggressive, int8 with mixed fp16 activations.
[07:45] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[07:47] Emily Zhao: Back to audit logs — will the logs contain prompt full text in private? I know you said configurable, but we need an assurance.
[07:55] Lena Park: For private deployments, logs can be configured to omit full prompt text, store hashed pointers, or store plaintext depending on your policy. We'll produce a config matrix.
[08:05] Marcus Chen: Also note our Optimize toolkit can recommend cache/batching knobs based on observed QPS patterns — it suggested the TTL bump we used. We'll share the recommendation output.
[08:15] Aisha Rahman: Ok in terms of timeline: we want Diego's 10k eval completed, Redwood to run the extra two tuning experiments, and then the final cost model. After that, the exec readout. Are we comfortable with 10/9? Sorry I meant 9/25 for the exec?
[08:29] Lena Park: Yes 2025-09-25 is the tentative exec readout. We'll lock once Diego confirms the eval.
[08:35] Diego Torres: I'll confirm dataset slice by 2025-09-16 and aim to have the 10k eval done by 2025-09-17 morning.
[08:41] Marcus Chen: I'll run the two additional tuning experiments (mixed fp16 profile + a TTL sweep for KV cache) and post results by EOD 2025-09-17.
[08:49] Aisha Rahman: Security will need the whitepaper and DPA before the exec readout. Emily, can you take the lead?
[08:56] Emily Zhao: Yes I'll compile questions and will need the specific endpoints and retention config.
[09:02] Lena Park: Action recap: send artifacts (benchmarks, cost model, security whitepaper), schedule exec readout for 2025-09-25, and finalize success criteria doc.
[09:12] Marcus Chen: One last note — competitor question: you asked about Anthropic earlier. Their trade is model safety vs performance; we think Redwood's routing and fallback gives you a deterministic cost and latency advantage.
[09:24] Aisha Rahman: Ok great. Any final blockers?
[09:27] Samir Patel: Finance wants the monthly delta including license and any reserved commitments — please surface early termination terms too.
[09:35] Lena Park: Noted. We'll include termination and contract term options.
[09:39] Carlos Mendez: Ops question — does Redwood ship Terraform or CloudFormation snippets for the private deployment?
[09:45] Marcus Chen: Yes, we'll share Terraform modules and an install playbook for on-prem + VPC templates.
[09:51] Aisha Rahman: Perfect. If there are no other items we'll wrap. Thanks, everyone.
[09:56] Lena Park: Thanks all — will send notes and artifacts.
[10:00] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels; some words like "KV cache" transcribed phonetically "kay vee cash" in the auto notes. There are small pauses and overlaps that got collapsed.

Attachments referenced during call: "northbridge_pilot_benchmarks_2025-09-15.xlsx" (will be shared), "security_whitepaper_redwood_v2.pdf" (to be shared), "one-pager-business-case.pdf" (to be produced).

Recap (verbatim-ish):
- Customer success criteria still: accuracy parity (>95%), p95 <= 300ms for short-mid flows, unit cost under customer threshold.
- Redwood to run 2 extra tuning experiments and share configs.
- Diego to confirm eval slice and run 10k eval.
- Security to get whitepaper, KMS integration details, and DPA.
- Exec readout planned for 2025-09-25.
